LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy: For a law p on a finite alphabet, its Shannon entropy in nats is H(p) = −∑ₐ p(a) ln p(a), with a zero term for each outcome of probability zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_sum: The entropy of a finite law p equals the sum of −p(a) ln p(a) over all outcomes, with 0 ln 0 taken as zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_nonneg: The entropy of a finite probability law is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_equiv: Bijectively relabeling the outcomes of a finite law preserves its entropy.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_injec: Pushing a finite law through an injective map to another finite alphabet preserves its entropy.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_pure: On a finite alphabet, a law concentrated at one point has entropy zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_zero_i: A finite probability law has entropy zero if and only if it is concentrated at one outcome.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf: For a finite-valued random variable X and discrete source law p, H(X) is the entropy of the distribution of X induced by p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_eq_zero: Let p be a probability mass function on the source outcomes and X a finite-valued random variable. Then H(X) = 0 exactly when there is a value a such that X(ω) = a for every ω with p(ω) > 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_id: For a finite law p, the entropy of the identity observation is H(p).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_comp_eq: Bijectively relabeling the finite values of a random variable X preserves H(X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_comp_in: If f is injective between finite alphabets, H(f(X)) = H(X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropy: For a pair of finite random quantities, the joint entropy is the entropy of their pair law, H(X,Y) = −∑ₓ,ᵧ p(x,y) ln p(x,y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_swap: Swapping the coordinates of a finite pair law leaves its entropy unchanged.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_prodA: Regrouping a finite triple from ((x,y),z) to (x,(y,z)) preserves its entropy.
Regrouping a finite triple from (x,(y,z)) to ((x,y),z) preserves its entropy.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropy_map_: The joint entropy of a finite pair law is unchanged when its coordinates are interchanged.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf: For finite-valued variables X and Y on the same discrete source, H(X,Y) is the entropy of the random pair (X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_sw: For finite-valued X and Y under the same law, H(Y,X) = H(X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_prodAss: For jointly defined finite-valued X, Y and Z, the variables (X,(Y,Z)) and ((X,Y),Z) have the same entropy.
